fix_commit_message:
avfilter/buffersink: don't leak the reallocated channel layouts array

And ensure the last element is the zeroed terminator.

Fixes ticket #11392.

Signed-off-by: James Almer <jamrial@gmail.com>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 041a6c36142f on top of intro b8bf2f4e1758 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (NullPointerDereference): In common_init(), when parsing channel layouts from the deprecated 'ch_layouts' option string, av_realloc_array() is called to grow buf->channel_layouts. The return value is stored in the local variable 'tmp', but is never assigned back to buf->channel_layouts. Since av_realloc_array() may free the original buffer and return a pointer to a newly allocated buffer (or return a new allocation when the original pointer is NULL), buf->channel_layouts remains stale (NULL on the first iteration, or a dangling pointer on subsequent iterations). The immediately following memset() on line 208 dereferences buf->channel_layouts, causing a null pointer dereference crash (SEGV). Additionally, the memset only zeroes sizeof(*buf->channel_layouts) bytes (one element) instead of sizeof(*buf->channel_layouts) * 2 bytes (the new element plus the terminator), leaving the terminator element uninitialized. This is triggered by filter graphs containing abuffersink with channel layout options, e.g. 'abuffersink=::a'. Root cause: After calling av_realloc_array() to grow the channel_layouts array, the new pointer stored in 'tmp' was never assigned back to buf->channel_layouts. This is a classic realloc pattern bug where the caller forgets to update the original pointer. On the first iteration, buf->channel_layouts is NULL, so the memset writes to address 0x0. On subsequent iterations, if realloc moved the buffer, buf->channel_layouts becomes a dangling pointer (use-after-free). A secondary issue is that the memset only clears one element instead of two (the new entry plus the zero terminator).
